reasons.A: Formal, dryly ironic diction and a parenthetical aside come near the author, but the first-person 'I' and the neat, polished short-sentence rhythm drift from the passage's awkward, inverted editorial movement.
reasons.B: Plain, earnest, warmly confiding first-person memoir. It has none of the passage's mock-formal irony, editorial 'we' or stiff, circuitous syntax, so it reads most like a different writer.
reasons.C: Keeps the editorial 'we', the mock-solemn formality ('We did not undeceive him'), the ironic distance and the dash-broken dialogue. Its rhythm is closest to the passage, though the aphoristic asides ('Just so.') lean a little towards the essayistic.
